The answer is $\lambda = 48$, attained by placing the 12 points at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side 1, four points at each vertex.

**Reduction.** Let $G$ be the centroid of the points and $O$ any point. Then

$$\sum_{i<j}|P_iP_j|^2 = 12\sum_{i}|P_i-G|^2,$$

and since $\sum_i|P_i-O|^2 = \sum_i|P_i-G|^2 + 12|G-O|^2$, we have $\sum_i|P_i-G|^2 \le \sum_i|P_i-O|^2$ for every $O$.

**Jung's theorem.** A planar set of diameter $1$ lies in a disk of radius $1/\sqrt3$. Take $O$ to be the center of that disk. Then $|P_i-O|^2\le 1/3$ for all $i$, so

$$\sum_{i<j}|P_iP_j|^2 \le 12\sum_i|P_i-O|^2 \le 12\cdot 12\cdot\tfrac13 = 48.$$

**Attainment.** Put 4 points at each vertex of an equilateral triangle with side 1. Every pair of points is at distance $0$ or $1$, so the diameter condition holds. The pairs at distance 1 number $4\cdot4\cdot 3 = 48$, so the sum is $48$.

Hence the smallest $\lambda$ is $48$.

ANSWER: 48
